fixture_name: Ramp-terminal arterial reconstruction — US preliminary design (MassDOT HSIP municipal RSA, full package)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Missing delineated/accessible crossings at ramp terminals plus a non-compliant four-lane mid-block crossing with a recorded pedestrian fatality is core preliminary-design RSA subject matter with clear severity and exposure potential.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Verbatim FHWA quotes (EV-US-030 separation-failure mechanism, EV-US-032 signing/marking duty) directly support the pivotal claim, while site conditions trace to recorded Safety Issue #4 observations; no invented content detected.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: US/FHWA semantics respected: safety concern remains the categorical frame with MUTCD/ADA items as supporting observations, and recommendations are correctly staged for preliminary design ('as part of the current design', future-signal provision).
justifications.recommendation_quality: Four specific, phased, viable measures—immediate MUTCD signage upgrade, design-stage ADA ramps and designated crosswalks, future signalized ramp crossings, and sidewalk-linked relocation to the Derby Shoppes signal—each mapped to an identified risk.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians, the directly exposed vulnerable road user group, are comprehensively treated across exposure, sightlines, physical/temporal separation, and crash history, with divided driver attention also acknowledged.

justifications.substance: Undefined lane drop with abrupt striping termination and no advance signage creating late merges at an on-ramp mouth is a classic FHWA-RSA driver-expectancy/decision-load issue squarely in scope at preliminary design stage, with a credible vehicle-vehicle conflict mechanism against ramp-exiting turning traffic.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claims (striping ends abruptly at the Old Derby Street crosswalk; no advance signage; observed late merges) are anchored by verbatim quoted field observations in EV-US-033, with EV-US-023 correctly framing the RSA purpose, and inference (expectancy/collision potential) is explicitly labelled rather than presented as evidence.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly typed as a safety_concern grounded in operational/design characteristics per the FHWA RSA framing, with no drift into compliance assertions; the null normative_basis_note is appropriate since no code requirement is invoked.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: advance merge signage plus pavement markings ahead of the on-ramp, with a viable design-stage alternative (extend two through lanes past the ramp entrance with signed mandatory-right-turn trade-off) carried into the ongoing reconstruction.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not part of this finding's merging/turning conflict mechanism, but the finding explicitly acknowledges pedestrians at the adjacent mid-block crosswalk affected by diverted driver attention and delegates that impact to JB-GF12-001.
